testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is a problem with transporting hanging meat?

options.text: It should never be transported by trailer.
It can be an unstable load.
It must be approved by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be an unstable load.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat creates an unstable load. It has a high center of gravity, and the meat can swing. This swinging affects how the driver can control the vehicle.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
It turns on the air compressor.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when air is pumped into the storage tanks. It stops pumping if pressure gets too high. It starts pumping if pressure gets too low.

questions.question: What is a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer
The rating of a combination vehicle per axle

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle as set by the manufacturer.

questions.question: When you apply the brakes, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle pulls to one side.
The vehicle does not pull to either side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle does not pull to either side.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when you brake, there may be a problem with the brakes.

questions.question: How do you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Turn on the engine and apply the trailer hand brake.
Press and release the brake pedal quickly and repeatedly.
Remove wheel chocks and disengage the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and release the brake pedal quickly and repeatedly.
questions.explanation: After the system has charged, test the warning signal by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air from the brake system. The warning signal should come on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to function?
questions.explanation: Air brakes work by using compressed air.

questions.question: What should warning lights and buzzers do when you start a vehicle?

options.text: They should not light up or sound.
They should turn on and then shut off quickly.
They should turn on and stay on.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should turn on and then shut off quickly.
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, warning lights and buzzers should turn on briefly and then turn off quickly.

questions.question: How much should a slack adjuster move from where it attaches to the push rod?
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check each slack adjuster. Pull on them to make sure they move no more than about one inch from where the push rod is attached. If they move more than one inch, they are out of adjustment and need to be fixed.

questions.question: What is the number one cause of death and injury in a work zone?
questions.explanation: Speeding causes the most deaths and injuries in work zones. Be extra careful when driving near workers.

questions.question: Which item is not required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and a fire extinguisher. A flashlight is optional.

questions.question: When making a left turn, when should you start the turn?

options.text: Before you reach the center of the intersection.
At or after you reach the center of the intersection.
After your rear wheels pass the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or after you reach the center of the intersection.
questions.explanation: Wait until you reach the center of the intersection before turning left. If you turn too early, the left side of your vehicle may hit another vehicle.

questions.question: What are alcohol evaporators?

options.text: Devices that add alcohol to air brake systems.
Only allowed in the northern parts of the state.

questions.correctAnswerText: Devices that add alcohol to air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have alcohol evaporators. They add alcohol to the braking system to prevent ice from forming.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Do not use your turn signals.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signals and check your mirrors when changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do before driving downhill?

options.text: Take your vehicle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift into a lower gear before going downhill. This prevents you from overusing your brakes.

questions.question: How should you brake in a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: Pump the brakes several times before pressing hard on the pedal.
Press the brake pedal as hard as possible every time you slow or stop.

questions.explanation: Brake the same way in an ABS vehicle as in a regular vehicle. ABS automatically works when needed to prevent the wheels from locking up.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle fits under a bridge or sign, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Slow down if you are not sure your vehicle will fit under overhead objects. Take a different route if possible.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Speed up and slow down frequently.
Change your driving to fit the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your driving to fit the weather.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, adjust your speed to match conditions. Your vehicle takes longer to stop on slippery roads. Increase your following distance and avoid frequent speed changes.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air tank drains?

options.text: Only to use when it is wet outside.
To remove all water and oil from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: To remove all water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and compressor oil from air brake system tanks. Always drain the tanks completely.

questions.question: How often should you inspect cargo during a trip?

options.text: Only after the trip is finished.
Every time you take a break.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you take a break.
questions.explanation: Inspect your cargo and how it is secured every time you take a break. Also inspect it at least every 150 miles.

questions.question: What is hanging meat as cargo usually like?
questions.explanation: Hanging meat cargo is unstable because the meat swings while the vehicle moves and its center of gravity is high.

questions.question: What is a tire load?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a specific pressure.

questions.question: A distracted driver:

options.text: Usually follows the rules of the road.
Is a good person to follow.

questions.explanation: Distracted drivers notice hazards on the road more slowly than focused drivers. They may not see hazards at all.

questions.question: When trying to put out an electrical fire, you should:
questions.explanation: B:C fire extinguishers work on electrical fires and burning liquids. Never use water on an electrical fire.

questions.question: If a vehicle is carrying hazardous cargo, placards must be placed:

options.text: Only on the front of the vehicle.
On the front, rear, and sides of the vehicle.
Only on the driver's side of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, rear, and sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Placards must be on the front, rear, and both sides of a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo. They must be visible from all directions.

questions.question: When a vehicle is started, the coolant temperature should:
questions.explanation: When an engine starts, the coolant temperature should rise gradually to a normal operating range.

questions.question: When traveling down a downgrade, the speed of a vehicle will likely:
questions.explanation: Gravity causes a vehicle to speed up when traveling downhill.

questions.question: How should you brake if your vehicle's ABS is not working?

options.text: Brake normally, as you will still have functioning brakes.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally, as you will still have functioning brakes.
questions.explanation: Without a working Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), your vehicle still has normal brakes. Drive and brake as you normally would, and get your ABS fixed as soon as possible.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle, you should not:

options.text: Park in an area away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Notify emergency services of your problem and your location.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop in an open area. Do not go to a service station—fuel there could catch fire. Call emergency services and tell them your location.

questions.question: A dual air brake system:

options.text: Consists of two separate air brake systems that share a single set of controls.
Is a single air brake system with two different sets of controls.
Consists of one air brake system for the left side of the truck and one system for the right side of the truck, each with its own set of controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Consists of two separate air brake systems that share a single set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. They share one set of brake controls, but each has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. Usually one system controls the rear brakes and the other controls the front brakes.

questions.question: Livestock:

options.text: Should never be carried on a trailer.
Should be placed in the front of a trailer.

questions.explanation: Live animals can lean during turns and move during transport, which causes unstable weight distribution. Driving with livestock requires extra care.

questions.question: If the ABS light comes on while driving, what does it mean?

options.text: The ABS cannot work due to weather.
The ABS has just been activated.
The ABS is not working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: The ABS warning light means something in the anti-lock braking system is not working properly.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle parked unattended, what should you do?

options.text: Use the parking brake only if parked on a slope.
Do not use the parking brake, as it can damage the tires.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when parking your vehicle. Do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if they are wet and it is freezing.

questions.question: When exiting a bus, what must a driver do?
questions.explanation: When exiting a bus, you must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. You must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may result in failing the vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: Do not drive if any brake drum has cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check the brake drums before driving. It is unsafe to drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: What is a problem with loading cargo improperly?
questions.explanation: Proper loading of cargo is essential for safety. Improperly loaded cargo can damage the vehicle and cause injury or death if it falls off during a collision or sudden stop.

questions.question: Is texting while operating a CMV illegal?

options.text: No, it is acceptable on rural roads.
No, it is acceptable when contacting your employer.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous and illegal for CMV operators.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while driving?
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and get sleep. Do not try to fight fatigue or use stimulants. These can cause fatal crashes.

questions.question: Why should flares be used with caution after an accident?

options.text: Fuel may be spilled on the ground and could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see the flares if it is sunny.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fuel may be spilled on the ground and could catch fire.
questions.explanation: Flares can start fires if there is spilled fuel nearby. Use them with caution after an accident.

questions.question: Which item is required emergency equipment for a commercial vehicle?
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, reflective triangles or flares, and a charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What is required to get a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: Provide fingerprints and pass a background check.
Provide employment history from the last five years.
Provide a list of countries visited in the last 10 years.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide fingerprints and pass a background check.
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must submit your fingerprints and pass a background check.

questions.question: When entering traffic, a large vehicle usually needs:

options.text: About the same space as a car.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more space to enter or cross traffic than smaller vehicles. The vehicle is larger and needs a longer distance to speed up.

questions.question: If convicted of a traffic violation (not a parking violation), you must:

options.text: Place a sign on the back of your vehicle about the conviction.
Lose your CDL for six months.

questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic violation conviction. You must also tell your motor vehicle agency within 30 days if the conviction happened in another state. Parking violations do not require notification.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery when it first begins to rain because:

options.text: Rain mixes with oil on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: When it first rains, the water mixes with oil drippings on the road. This creates a slippery, dangerous surface.

questions.question: Why should you do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time?

options.text: You will be less likely to forget to check something.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget to check something.
questions.explanation: Using the same steps each time helps you remember to inspect everything important.

questions.question: A truck's weight:

options.text: Usually has no effect on stopping distance.
Is a major factor in stopping distance.
Is less important than the type of cargo for stopping distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a major factor in stopping distance.
questions.explanation: A truck's weight greatly affects how far it takes to stop. Heavier vehicles need more braking power to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: Emergency equipment, such as fire extinguishers:

options.text: Are only needed for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Are only needed for interstate travel.
Are required in all commercial motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required in all commercial motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment, including fire extinguishers.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery right after it begins to rain because:

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Tires are not made for wet weather.
Water has not yet absorbed the dirt and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When it first rains, water mixes with oil and grease on the road that has not washed away yet. This creates a slick surface.

questions.question: When should you turn off a retarder for safety?

options.text: When you are carrying a heavy load.

questions.explanation: A retarder slows a vehicle without using the brakes. But on wet, snowy, or icy roads, it can cause wheels to skid. Turn off the retarder in these conditions.

questions.question: If the brakes pull to one side when used:
questions.explanation: If brakes pull to one side, there is a brake problem that needs to be fixed.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, the safest driving speed is:

options.text: The same speed as surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. If all vehicles move at the same speed in the same direction, they cannot crash into each other.
